source_cards.front: How should you treat railroad barriers and an approaching train?
source_cards.back: Obey railroad crossing warnings; never drive around a crossing barrier or try to outrun an approaching train.

source_cards.front: What space must be available beyond the tracks before you enter?
source_cards.back: Enter railroad tracks only when the far side has enough space to hold your entire vehicle.

source_cards.front: What gear-changing precaution applies to a manual vehicle crossing tracks?
source_cards.back: For a manual-transmission vehicle, avoid changing gears on railroad tracks to reduce the chance of an engine stall.

source_cards.front: How can the advance railroad warning sign be recognized?
source_cards.back: The round yellow railroad warning sign uses black markings and appears before a public highway-rail crossing.

source_cards.front: What should you do at an advance railroad warning?
source_cards.back: At an advance railroad warning sign, reduce speed, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop if one is approaching.

source_cards.front: Which pavement symbols warn of railroad tracks?
source_cards.back: Railroad pavement warnings include an X and the letters RR, with a no-passing marking on a two-lane road.

source_cards.front: What stopping marker may appear before the tracks?
source_cards.back: A white stop line may be painted on the approach side of railroad tracks.

source_cards.front: What is the railroad crossbuck's shape and color?
source_cards.back: The railroad crossbuck is a white X-shaped sign with black lettering located at the crossing.

source_cards.front: What right-of-way duty does the crossbuck impose?
source_cards.back: A railroad crossbuck requires drivers to give trains the right of way.

source_cards.front: What must a school bus do at a railroad crossing?
source_cards.back: School buses are required to stop when they reach railroad crossings.

source_cards.front: How do railroad pavement warnings relate to the advance warning sign?
source_cards.back: Railroad pavement markings give the same advance warning about a crossing as the round warning sign.

source_cards.front: May a driver go around a lowered crossing gate?
source_cards.back: Never attempt to drive around a lowered railroad crossing gate.

source_cards.front: May you cross flashing railroad lights if no train is visible?
source_cards.back: Do not cross railroad tracks while the red crossing lights flash, even if no train is visible.

source_cards.front: What check is needed at a crossing without a safety barrier?
source_cards.back: At a railroad crossing without a safety barrier, check for trains in both directions before crossing.

source_cards.front: Whom does the crossing emergency-notification sign help you contact?
source_cards.back: An emergency-notification sign provides contact information for the railroad responsible for the crossing.

source_cards.front: Why does the emergency-notification sign identify the particular crossing?
source_cards.back: Emergency-notification sign information identifies the particular railroad crossing so an emergency can be reported accurately.

source_cards.front: How may the red lights beside a crossbuck flash?
source_cards.back: Some railroad crossings have red lights positioned beside a crossbuck that flash alternately.

source_cards.front: Where is the yellow EXEMPT sign described in the guide positioned?
source_cards.back: One displayed form of an EXEMPT railroad sign has black lettering on a yellow background below an advance warning sign.

source_cards.front: Where is the white EXEMPT sign described in the guide positioned?
source_cards.back: The other displayed EXEMPT railroad sign has black lettering on white and appears below the crossbuck.

source_cards.front: What additional hazard exists at a multiple-track crossing?
source_cards.back: At a crossing with multiple railroad tracks, watch for another train approaching from either direction.

source_cards.front: When should you cross multiple tracks after a train passes?
source_cards.back: After a train passes a multiple-track crossing, wait until it is well away down the tracks before crossing.

source_cards.front: May you stop or park on railroad tracks?
source_cards.back: Do not stop or park a vehicle on railroad tracks.

source_cards.front: Where should you look when approaching a rail crossing?
source_cards.back: Look along the track in both directions whenever you approach a railroad crossing.

source_cards.front: Does never having seen a train at a crossing make it safe to assume none will come?
source_cards.back: Expect a train even at a crossing where you have never previously seen one.

source_cards.front: What does a multiple-tracks warning tell you about possible trains?
source_cards.back: Signs announcing multiple tracks warn that more than one train may use the crossing.

source_cards.front: Does one train passing prove every track is clear?
source_cards.back: A train that has just passed does not establish that all other tracks are clear.

source_cards.front: Do railroad signals still control at a familiar crossing?
source_cards.back: All railroad crossing signals must be obeyed, including at a familiar crossing.

source_cards.front: Who faces temporary hazards from roadway construction and maintenance?
source_cards.back: Highway construction and maintenance can create temporary hazards for drivers as well as the people working beside the road.

source_cards.front: What speed and lane restrictions may appear in a work zone?
source_cards.back: Work zones can have reduced speed limits and restrictions on which lanes may be used.

source_cards.front: Which speed limit applies when no work-zone reduction is posted?
source_cards.back: When a work zone has no posted speed reduction, obey the roadway's normally posted limit.

source_cards.front: How long may a standard work zone remain at one location?
source_cards.back: A standard construction work zone may stay at one location for months or years.

source_cards.front: How does a mobile work zone change location or stop?
source_cards.back: A mobile work zone involves short-duration work at a location and may move slowly between periodic stops.

source_cards.front: Which maintenance tasks can create a mobile work zone?
source_cards.back: Road striping, removal of road debris, and pothole patching are examples of work that can create a mobile work zone.

source_cards.front: What do flashing green construction or maintenance lights indicate?
source_cards.back: Flashing green lights on roadway construction or maintenance vehicles indicate an active work zone, calling for caution and a lower speed.

source_cards.front: Who is the flagger in a work area?
source_cards.back: A flagger is a person who directs work-area traffic using a flag or sign.

source_cards.front: When does the work-zone double-fine rule apply?
source_cards.back: When workers are present, a moving traffic violation in a work zone carries double the usual fine.

source_cards.front: Does the double-fine rule also apply to a mobile work zone?
source_cards.back: The double-fine rule applies to both mobile work zones and stationary work zones when workers are present.

source_cards.front: What should you do with a phone if no hands-free connection is available?
source_cards.back: In a work zone, leave the phone unused if you cannot operate it through a hands-free connection.

source_cards.front: When should you slow for work-zone signs and resume a changed limit?
source_cards.back: Begin slowing when signs announce a work zone or reduced work-zone speed, and keep the reduced speed until a posted speed-limit sign tells you otherwise.

source_cards.front: What route preparation helps before a trip through possible work zones?
source_cards.back: Before a trip, check whether work zones affect your route and consider an available alternative route.

source_cards.front: How should you reduce distractions before entering the work zone?
source_cards.back: Before entering a work zone, put your phone away and lower the radio so your attention stays on driving.

source_cards.front: What should you watch for inside a work zone?
source_cards.back: Inside a work zone, watch for workers, machinery, cones, barrels, and changed traffic paths.

source_cards.front: Why should you preserve following distance in work zones?
source_cards.back: Maintain adequate space behind the next vehicle because rear-end crashes are common in work zones.

source_cards.front: Which work-zone directions and controls must you obey?
source_cards.back: Obey work-zone warning signs and directions given by flaggers, cones, and barrels.

source_cards.front: Where are mobile work-zone identifying signs mounted?
source_cards.back: Mobile work zones use signs mounted on the back of transportation-department vehicles to identify the work zone.

source_cards.front: Where can an officer be positioned when using interstate work-zone cameras?
source_cards.back: In Arkansas interstate work zones, an officer can use a speed-enforcement camera to observe violations while positioned at the work zone's end.

source_cards.front: How can work-zone camera enforcement reduce the officer's exposure?
source_cards.back: Work-zone camera enforcement lets an officer stop a violator as the vehicle leaves, reducing the need for the officer to stand inside the work zone.

source_cards.front: Which warning signs and flashing light colors may identify mobile work?
source_cards.back: A mobile work zone may have work-ahead signs and work vehicles flashing green, yellow, or white lights.

source_cards.front: How long should you keep watching work-zone signs?
source_cards.back: Continue observing work-zone signs until you have left the entire work zone.

source_cards.front: How do flagger directions relate to other traffic controls?
source_cards.back: A work-zone flagger's signs or signals take priority over other traffic-control devices.

source_cards.front: Where should you stop for a flagger and when should you proceed?
source_cards.back: Stop at the place directed by a flagger, or remain at least one car length from the flagger, and wait for instructions to move.

source_cards.front: How can one lane carry opposing work-zone traffic?

source_cards.front: When should you avoid passing a cyclist?
source_cards.back: Do not pass a cyclist where the road is too narrow or the pass would force the rider dangerously close to parked vehicles.

source_cards.back: If a cyclist on a narrow road appears unaware of your approach, the guide recommends only a brief, gentle horn tap rather than a startling blast.

source_cards.back: Because bicycles are hard to see and offer no enclosure, riders are exposed and easily injured in a crash.

source_cards.back: Because bicycles are difficult to spot in traffic, oncoming bicycle traffic is frequently overlooked by motorists.

source_cards.front: Where should you watch for bicycles in residential areas?
source_cards.back: In residential areas, watch for bicyclists entering from driveways, behind parked vehicles, or other obstructions.

source_cards.front: Why do child cyclists require extra attention?
source_cards.back: Children riding bicycles may make sudden movements or changes of direction, requiring extra driver attention.

source_cards.back: At night, bicycles need a front lamp and rear reflector, but drivers must still watch carefully because cyclists are hard to see.

source_cards.front: Why might a tractor-trailer first move left before turning right?
source_cards.back: A tractor-trailer may first move left to create enough room for a right turn.

source_cards.front: Why is a tractor-trailer more than simply a larger car?
source_cards.back: A tractor-trailer is not simply a larger passenger car; its capabilities and normal maneuvers require different expectations from nearby drivers.

source_cards.front: What front blind area does the guide describe near a tractor-trailer cab?
source_cards.back: A passenger car may be hidden from a tractor-trailer's driver within twenty feet ahead of the cab.

source_cards.front: Where do tractor-trailer side blind spots extend?
source_cards.back: Tractor-trailer blind spots extend along both sides, especially near the cab.

source_cards.front: How far can the guide's described rear truck blind area extend?
source_cards.back: The guide describes the blind area behind a tractor-trailer as extending as far as two hundred feet.

source_cards.front: How should you pass a tractor-trailer?
source_cards.back: Pass a tractor-trailer on its left and complete the pass without lingering alongside.

source_cards.front: Why should a truck's approach be judged carefully?
source_cards.back: Judge the approach of a tractor-trailer carefully; its size can make it appear to move more slowly than it actually does.

source_cards.front: What passenger-car-side share does the guide attribute in its cited fatal multivehicle tractor-trailer comparison?
source_cards.back: The guide attributes seventy-two percent of fatal multivehicle crashes involving a tractor-trailer to the passenger-car side in its cited national comparison.
